source: The Resilient Path by Pendleton B. Wickersham, MD (© 2025)

messages.text: You are not powerless. You are not just your illness.
You get to decide what you carry, what you let go, and what you fight for.
Resilience isn't about being unbreakable — it's about being creative and compassionate with yourself.
The only thing I can control is how I approach things.
Hurt does not always equal harm.
Knowledge truly is power.
Start low, go slow.
Consistency over heroics.
Celebrate your small victories.
You are the most important member of your team.
Acknowledge progress, not perfection.
Even in pain, we are still powerful.
Your life is still yours to shape.
We are stronger than we realize.
You are capable of growing through it.
The shift that changes everything: from “fix it or fail” to “live it and adapt.”
Life isn't just about avoiding pain — it's about recognizing what's worth facing it for.
Embrace what you can control: your mindset, your actions, your willingness to adapt.
No matter what happens to us, we are capable of facing it.
Pain may be part of your life, but it doesn't get to write your whole story.
You can begin a new chapter — not pain-free, but full of purpose.
Laughter may not be a cure, but it's an anchor.
Sometimes you can't change the pain — but you can bob and weave around it.
It's not easy — but it's possible.
You are a whole person — not a list of symptoms, not a case to be solved.
You are the expert on your own body and your own experience.
You are not a passive recipient of care — you are the active partner in it.
Your journey may be complex, but understanding leads to healing.
Acknowledging how you feel is a courageous first step on the road to healing.
Be true to who you are, even as that “who” evolves.
You can discover new strengths, and find value in new ways of being.
Focus on what can be changed — and reclaim the parts of life that hold meaning and joy.
Never underestimate the power of informed self-management.
Respect your pain, and still find safe ways to keep moving.
